system_prompt:
You are a senior systems architect compiling a dense Architectural Fact Sheet from project documents.
Compile:
1. Core Business Goals (exactly 5 specific items)
2. Primary User Personas & Entry Points
3. Identified Pain Points & Constraints (exactly 5 specific items)
4. Key Technology Stack preferences (Frontend, Backend, DB)
5. Critical Security & Performance NFRs

Return ONLY valid JSON with these fields. No explanations.
user_prompt:
BRD:


TECH SUMMARY:
["Single-page web app (SPA) built with Bootstrap 5.3.3; frontend-first architecture, browser-deployable with no heavy dependencies", "Backend pipeline resides entirely in server.py; Python-based with scikit-learn and Azure AI Foundry integrations", "Input: Excel or CSV PowerBI metadata uploads via drag-and-drop; output: exportable Excel governance reports", "Data model is a per-report attribute dictionary mapping report names to lists of field/measure/dimension strings", "Two-stage AI/ML pipeline: local hybrid scoring (TF-IDF, Jaccard, Levenshtein) followed by LLM semantic scoring", "LLM is Meta Llama 3.3 70B Instruct accessed via Azure AI Foundry using AzureOpenAI client instantiated per-request", "TF-IDF vectorizer is character-level (bi-gram to 4-gram), fit fresh per request \u2014 not persisted or pre-trained", "LLM inference batches 25 attribute pairs per call, parallelised via ThreadPoolExecutor (max_workers=2) with retry/backoff", "Preprocessing normalises Unicode anomalies, strips whitespace, and lowercases all attribute strings before scoring", "UI constraints: max-width 1200px content area, responsive breakpoints at 768px and 480px, purple-themed design system", "NFR: deterministic LLM output enforced via low temperature (0.1) and strict JSON-only prompt instructions", "Positioned as a zero-infrastructure governance tool for large PowerBI estates with inconsistent cross-team naming"]

core_business_goals: Automate governance reporting for large PowerBI estates with inconsistent cross-team naming conventions
Identify and surface duplicate or semantically similar attributes across PowerBI reports at scale
Produce exportable Excel governance reports from PowerBI metadata with minimal manual effort
Eliminate infrastructure overhead by delivering a zero-infrastructure, browser-deployable governance tool
Enforce deterministic, auditable AI-driven attribute matching to support data governance compliance

personas.name: Data Governance Analyst
personas.description: Responsible for auditing and standardising PowerBI report metadata across teams; primary consumer of governance reports
personas.entry_point: Drag-and-drop Excel/CSV PowerBI metadata upload on the SPA landing interface

personas.name: BI Platform Administrator
personas.description: Manages large PowerBI estates across multiple teams; needs cross-report attribute consistency visibility
personas.entry_point: Direct browser access to the SPA; uploads metadata exports from PowerBI tenants

entry_points: Browser-based SPA accessed directly with no login or infrastructure setup
Drag-and-drop file upload accepting Excel or CSV PowerBI metadata exports
Exportable Excel governance report download as the primary output delivery mechanism

identified_pain_points_and_constraints: Inconsistent cross-team naming conventions across PowerBI estates make manual attribute reconciliation infeasible at scale
No existing zero-infrastructure tooling exists to perform semantic governance analysis without heavy deployment overhead
LLM inference latency risk due to per-request client instantiation and batched parallel calls to Azure AI Foundry
TF-IDF vectorizer is fit fresh per request and not persisted, introducing recomputation overhead on every upload
LLM non-determinism risk requires mitigation via low temperature settings and strict JSON-only prompt constraints to ensure auditable outputs

frontend: Frontend-first, browser-deployable with no heavy dependencies
Responsive design: max-width 1200px, breakpoints at 768px and 480px
backend: Azure AI Foundry integration via AzureOpenAI client
Hybrid scoring: TF-IDF + Jaccard + Levenshtein (local) followed by LLM semantic scoring
database: No persistent database; per-request in-memory attribute dictionary (report name to field/measure/dimension string lists)
Input: Excel or CSV file uploads

critical_security_and_performance_nfrs: Deterministic LLM output enforced via low temperature (0.1) and strict JSON-only prompt instructions to ensure auditable governance results
LLM inference batched at 25 attribute pairs per call with retry/backoff logic to handle Azure AI Foundry transient failures
Parallelised LLM calls via ThreadPoolExecutor capped at max_workers=2 to balance throughput against API rate limits
Unicode normalisation and input sanitisation (whitespace stripping, lowercasing) applied to all attribute strings before scoring to prevent data quality and injection issues
Zero-infrastructure deployment model requires all processing to be self-contained with no persistent server-side state, minimising attack surface and operational risk
